title: Dynamic Cooperative Energy and Coverage Management for V2G-Enhanced RAN Resilience.
abstract: he resilience of cellular communication is paramount, given how widely its services are used. However, it also depends on the resilience of the power grid, which is increasingly threatened by extreme weather events and the growing reliance on distributed, intermittent energy sources. Current base station backup systems, typically limited to 2-6 hours of autonomy, operate in isolation and fail to leverage spatial redundancy. This paper proposes the Multi-Site Resiliency Cooperative (MSRC) framework, a unified control strategy that transforms independent sites into a collaborative energy cluster. We formulate a two-stage mixed-integer optimization problem that jointly manages radio coverage adaptation switching sites between helping, assisted, and deep-sleep modes and dynamic Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) energy injection. By proactively reshaping cell boundaries and traffic loads based on real-time battery states, MSRC maximizes network survival while prioritizing critical service classes. Extensive simulations on a 19-site urban network demonstrate that the proposed framework extends survival time by 96% and maintains 94% service continuity compared to conventional baselines. Crucially, MSRC requires no physical in- frastructure upgrades, offering operators a deployable, software- defined solution for outage-resilient green communications.

title: Beyond Communication: On-Modem DNN Inference and Training for Home Appliances.
abstract: We introduce on-modem learning, which enables a commodity communication modem installed on commercial home appliances to perform inference and training of compact-sized DNNs (deep neural networks) to provide custom intelligent services. Given that 80-90% of commercial smart home appliances are never connected to the network, leaving computing resources of the modem idle, the proposed on-modem learning transforms a learning-incapable modem into an independent self-learning module by utilizing the unused or under-utilized modem resources. To this end, we propose an on-modem DNN inference framework consisting of Data Payload Parser and On-Modem DNN engine. We also propose an on-modem DNN training framework, which enables resource-efficient training of DNNs on the modem via Greedy and Diverse Gradient Accumulation (GDGA), Dynamic Programming-based Back-Propagation (DPBP), and On-Modem Reinforcement Learning (OMRL). To the best of our knowledge, the proposed on-modem learning is the first to execute DNN inference and training on the modem of commercial home appliances. To validate the efficacy of on-modem learning, we implement two on-modem learning applications on the real LG Electronics washing machine, i.e., (1) remaining wash time prediction and (2) UE (unbalance error) forecasting. Our experiment shows that on-modem learning successfully conducts DNN inference and training on the modem of commercial home appliances and provides custom intelligent services to end users.

title: Tiny-ish ML for Big Impact: How to Utilise EdgeAI in Software-Defined Vehicles.
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) algorithms are commonly used in vehicles as part of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) in time and safety-critical systems. Thus, maximising the speed of the algorithm and minimising latency while preserving the accuracy of the ML models is vitally important. At the same time, vehicles as edge devices are constrained environments with limited processing capabilities, power, and internet connectivity. However, algorithms for ADAS require a significant amount of processing power, and pure tinyML algorithms might become insufficient. Hence, there is a need to implement vehicular Edge AI. This paper outlines a research plan for evaluating different ML/AI distribution solutions in the vehicular environment, with a practical use case of object detection from FLIR ADK 2.0 thermal camera data on NVIDIA’s constrained edge device, the Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit. Additionally, the more demanding task of sensor fusion with lidar data is attempted. As a result, the latency and accuracy of different solutions will be evaluated within real-world use cases.

title: GAEA: Experiences and Lessons Learned from a Country-Scale Environmental Digital Twin.
abstract: This paper describes the experiences and lessons learned after the deployment of a country-scale environmental digital twin on the island of Cyprus for three years. This digital twin, called GAEA, contains 27 environmental geospatial services and is suitable for urban planners, policymakers, farmers, property owners, real-estate and forestry professionals, as well as insurance companies and banks that have properties in their portfolio. This paper demonstrates the power, potential, current and future challenges of geospatial analytics and environmental digital twins on a large scale.

title: Foreground Graphics-Aware Runtime DNN Scheduling on Mobile GPUs.
abstract: We propose GPUSched, a foreground graphics aware preemptive scheduling framework for concurrent DNN inference and seamless graphics rendering on mobile GPUs. Given that existing GPU scheduling methods relying on offline slicing are inadequate for dynamic graphics workloads, GPUSched is driven by two key components: (i) Render-State Detection via GPUPing, which leverages lightweight probing of GPU queue latency to accurately identify foreground rendering operations and (ii) Adaptive Operator Chunking, which dynamically fits DNN model chunk sizes within GPU idle times in a GPU frequency-aware manner. By combining these mechanisms GPUSched, coordinates DNN inference with graphics rendering in real time, preventing deadline violations while maximizing GPU utilization. Experiments on two commodity mobile devices show that GPUSched consistently outperforms baseline schedulers, achieving lower deadline miss rates while sustaining high rendering quality even under demanding graphics workload.

title: Selective Data Sharing for Digital Product Passports using Heterogeneous Twins.
abstract: Continuous evolution of digital products makes them generate vast amounts of lifecycle data, creating new demands for secure, transparent, and efficient data sharing across stakeholders. While the EU’s Digital Product Passport (DPP) initiative aims to address these challenges, current solutions lack robust architectures for secure, real-time, and selective data exchange, especially during the crucial middle-of-life (MOL) phase. This paper introduces a decentralized architecure where mini digital twins (mDT) project distinct product DT states for selective data disclosure, supporting multiple lifecycle stages and sustainable decision-making. Our approach demonstratesstakeholder-specific data sharing through heterogeneous mDT using OrbitDB, enabling low-latency lifecycle data access for Digital product passports.

title: Using a Smart Ring to Control Your Music Player.
abstract: Smart rings have become pervasive lifestyle gadgets. By providing an unobtrusive way to measure parameters like heart rate and blood oxygen saturation, they are frequently used to derive health-related factors like sleep scores and stress levels. Many smart rings, however, also contain an integrated three-axis accelerometer to differentiate between activity and rest periods. Acceleration data captured from tracking the human finger – if available at a sufficiently high sampling rate – can also be used to identify motions and gestures, though. We show this by way of using finger gestures to control a music player software. Our approach, called MusicRing, is capable of differentiating between six finger gestures when using a commodity smart ring, which is limited to a 4 Hz sampling rate. We will demonstrate how MusicRing can detect the music control gestures while standard office activities (e.g., typing on a keyboard or moving a mouse) are not recognized as control commands. This enables seamless music control while minimizing interruptions to office work.

title: Large Language Models Meet Wearable Sensing: A Demo of Training-Free HAR with RAG-HAR.
abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) underpins applications in healthcare, rehabilitation, fitness tracking, and smart environments, yet many existing approaches remain difficult to integrate into real applications due to their training requirements and computational overhead. This paper presents RAG-HAR, a training-free, retrieval-augmented HAR framework based on large language models (LLMs), implemented by the authors as a lightweight widget within an Android fitness application developed using the Flutter framework and Android Studio. The demonstration highlights the end-to-end integration of the RAG-HAR pipeline within a user-facing application, illustrating its operation under continuous sensor input and its suitability for practical health and fitness scenarios.

title: HyperEcho: Structured Higher Order Representation for Automotive Radar Semantic Segmentation.
abstract: Automotive radar is attractive for perception in adverse weather and lighting conditions, but semantic segmentation on radar maps is still difficult. Objects in radar heatmaps are sparse and noisy, appearing as extended blobs or streaks rather than neat contours. Most existing CNN and transformer backbones treat these maps like ordinary images and rely on local filters or pairwise attention, which makes it hard to capture the larger echo patterns that define objects. We propose HyperEcho, a backbone that is tailored to radar feature maps. Instead of reasoning only over individual pixels, HyperEcho builds a simple hypergraph on top of the feature map: it learns a few groups of positions along the range and angle/Doppler axes that each capture an echo pattern, runs a lightweight attention mechanism over these groups, and then propagates the result back to the underlying pixels. This axial hypergraph backbone can be used on its own or combined with a lightweight contrastive loss that encourages consistent features across radar views. On the CARRADA benchmark, HyperEcho consistently improves semantic segmentation over strong CNN and transformer baselines. Our best variant sets a new state of the art on both Range–Doppler and Range–Angle segmentation, achieving 62.4% mIoU on RD and 45.1% mIoU on RA, showing that explicitly modelling higher-order echo structure is beneficial for radar scene understanding.

title: Deployment Limits of Cross-Subject EEG Emotion Recognition: A Multimodal Baseline Study.
abstract: Understanding how well emotion recognition systems generalize across individuals is critical for affect-aware interfaces, pervasive sensing, and human-centered computing. This paper presents a deployment-aligned diagnostic study that measures cross-subject generalization limits for EEG-based affect sensing under strict unseen-user protocols. Using a unified mul-timodal baseline (Cross-Modal Attention Transformer, CMAT) with supervised contrastive learning (SupCon) as a consistent training objective, we evaluate the same pipeline across SEED-VII (EEG+eye; physiological), IEMOCAP (audio–video–text; behavioral control), and EAV (EEG–audio–video; hybrid) using leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) or speaker/session-independent splits. Results show strong modality dependence: IEMOCAP reaches 57.2% accuracy, while SEED-VII yields 18.97 ± 5.77% (Fusion) and 20.28 ± 3.73% (SupCon) under LOSO. Confusion-matrix and embedding analyses indicate that low-arousal emotions remain overlapping and unstable across subjects, whereas high-arousal states exhibit relatively more consistent structure. A calibration study further shows that naive personalization under extreme data scarcity can be counterproductive with < 20 labeled samples and becomes more stable around 20–30 samples per subject. These findings provide practical guidance for pervasive, human-centered emotion-aware systems regarding modality selection and calibration burden.

title: Dynamic Client Selector: A Double Deep Q-Learning Framework for Efficient Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a method for training a shared machine learning model without transferring raw data to a central server. This approach protects privacy while enabling collaborative learning. It is difficult to integrate FL with the Internet of Things (IoT). The computing power, communication capabilities, and network dependability of devices vary, as may the quality of the data they generate. We thus need reliable client selection techniques that choose the best devices to be included in the training process. This paper presents DCS, a client selection approach in FL using Double Deep Q-Learning (DDQL) that optimizes client choices based on factors such as trust, latency, and performance. Key innovations include a balanced scoring mechanism, utilizing a decay factor to prioritize recent updates, and incremental principal component analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction, ensuring only quality updates are integrated. Additionally, the Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search method is used for outlier detection, filtering out unreliable clients to enhance global model convergence and reduce computational costs. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method on two datasets, MNIST and CIFAR-10, in heterogeneous settings. On the MNIST dataset, the proposed approach achieved a final accuracy of 99.06%, surpassing existing methods named Favor, FLASH-RL, and FedAvg. Furthermore, on the Fashion-MNIST (IID), DCS achieves up to 89.5% test accuracy while converging in approximately 110–115 rounds.

title: Artifact: Now You See Me, Now You Don't: Consent-Driven Privacy for Smart Glasses.
abstract: This artifact provides the complete three-tier reference implementation, dataset subset, and evaluation code necessary to reproduce the experiments and results reported in the paper "Now You See Me, Now You Don’t: Consent-Driven Privacy for Smart Glasses" [1] . Tier 1 implements on-device face blurring and encryption to prevent exposure of raw facial pixels. Tier 2 provides wearers with an optional landmark-driven synthetic face replacement feature to preserve wearer utility. Finally, Tier 3 allows wearers to utilize a consent-mediated restoration protocol that returns original faces only after explicit bystander authorization. The repository includes the end-to-end capture pipeline, companion synthetic-replacement code, restoration and TTP simulation modules, evaluation notebooks, and a sampled dataset of 16,500 annotated frames. The artifact (including an extensive README.md file) can be publicly accessed using the following GitHub repository [2] . https://github.com/SYSNET-LUMS/SmartGlassesPrivacy

title: CHG-Net: A Unified Direction-Aware Graph Framework for Multi-Class Trajectory Prediction.
abstract: Accurate prediction of future trajectories in unstructured environments is essential for safe autonomous vehicle operation, especially when pedestrians, cyclists, and motor vehicles interact in complex and unpredictable ways. Many existing prediction models predict based on a single class or rely on multiple separate graphs for multi-class prediction. This work introduces a lightweight trajectory prediction framework that represents all agents within a single Comprehensive Heterogeneous Graph, enriched with a directional interaction mask that highlights behaviourally important neighbours based on relative distance, velocity, and motion direction. A spatial-temporal design combining a Spatial-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network with a micro Temporal Convolutional Network allows efficient modeling of motion dynamics, while a Gaussian mixture model decoder enables probabilistic training and deterministic maximum likelihood prediction for simulation. Experiments on the Stanford Drone Dataset show improved accuracy over recent multi-class baselines, and qualitative visualizations confirm stable, socially coherent, and scene-consistent predictions suitable for real-time autonomous systems.

title: Confidence-Based Maintenance Optimization in Digital Twins for Aging Sensor Networks.
abstract: Aging sensor networks within Digital Twin (DT) ecosystems pose increasing challenges for maintaining synchronization between physical and virtual environments. This paper presents a confidence-driven maintenance optimization framework that integrates probabilistic sensor modeling, inspection-route optimization, and interactive DT visualization.The proposed framework is implemented within a DT application. It visualizes sensor states and optimized inspection routes to support data-driven decision-making. Our framework is constructed from collected sensor data. Sensor relocation is modeled as a Poisson process and sensor lifetime is modeled as a Weibull distribution, and a confidence score is used to prioritize inspection targets. A routing algorithm optimizes the inspection sequence by balancing travel cost and sensor confidence-based priorities.A case study on a smart-campus environment demonstrates how varying relocation rates, lifetime shape and inspection intervals affect overall cost and system confidence outcomes. Results show that the proposed confidence-based inspection can reduce maintenance costs by over 50% compared to full inspection, while maintaining high system confidence. These findings offer actionable design insights for implementing DT Ecosystems in smart-building and industrial domains, highlighting how data-driven inspection strategies can optimize operational efficiency and resource allocation.

title: Static Code Analysis for Extracting Peripheral Device Knowledge in Pervasive Systems.
abstract: Pervasive and IoT systems increasingly rely on emulation frameworks to test embedded software, yet growing codebases make it challenging to ensure consistent and complete hardware models. This work-in-progress introduces a domain-specific static analysis method for the Renode emulator, using Roslyn-based analysers to automatically extract and validate peripheral register maps, reset logic, and structural patterns. The system provides diagnostics and machine-readable model descriptions, enabling automated documentation and cross-model comparison to support code reuse and hardware onboarding. Initial results show effective detection of modelling gaps and enforcement of implementation guidelines. Ongoing work focuses on extending analysis coverage and integrating these tools into continuous development workflows.

title: Edge-Based Well-Being Monitoring Using Non-Biometric Multimodal Digital Signals.
abstract: Digital well-being tools often rely on cloud analytics and biometric sensing, creating major privacy and ethical risks. We propose EWA (Edge-based Well-being Assistant), a fully edge-native, privacy-preserving system that infers emotional and behavioural well-being using non-biometric multimodal digital signals processed entirely on user devices. The system analyses behavioural patterns to estimate mood and stress trends while enforcing data minimisation and user autonomy. Results demonstrate that meaningful well-being insights can be achieved without intrusive biometrics or cloud dependence, highlighting edge-native approaches as a viable and ethical direction for digital well-being technologies.

title: High-Performance Robust Energy System Planning with Storage: A Single-LP Approach.
abstract: Effective design of resilient urban energy systems depends on decision-support tools that can evaluate options and guide planning in the face of uncertainty. We present a robust optimization framework for the Berlin–Brandenburg energy system based on the open-source oemof-B3 model. Our approach integrates up to 250 demand scenarios into a single large linear program, enabling the joint optimization of generation, sector coupling, and storage technologies under demand uncertainty. The resulting robust solution is compared against a solution catalog obtained by solving each scenario independently, illustrating the benefits and trade-offs of robust decision-making in urban energy planning. Despite the model’s scale, the linear program can be solved with commercial solvers within approximately one day. We explore state-of-the-art strategies to reduce computation time, comparing the performance of the specialized parallel interior-point solver PIPS-IPM++ on high-performance computing systems with emerging GPU-accelerated optimization approaches. By applying both methods to our large-scale Berlin–Brandenburg case study, we discuss their respective strengths and limitations and highlight how rapidly evolving GPU-based algorithms contrast with mature HPC-optimized solvers in terms of scalability, robustness, and solution quality.

title: TruFedSense: Trust-Aware Federated Learning for Multi-Fault Heterogeneous IoT Sensor Streams.
abstract: Reliability assessment in long-term, heterogeneous Internet-of-Things (IoT) deployments is crucial, as sensor data degrades over time, producing noise and faults. Label scarcity and distinct behavior (from one-to-multi-class) data among edge nodes are two critical issues. Existing federated learning (FL) methods often overlook these challenges in multi-fault class scenarios, focusing on adversarial attacks. Towards this, we propose TruFedSense, a trust-aware FL framework that estimates edge node reliability via Trust-weighted Averaging (TruFedAvg). TruFedSense uses a Long Short-Term Memory AutoEncoder (LSTM-AE) architecture to mitigate label scarcity and Gaussian-perturbed latents to enhance TruFedAvg privacy. TruFedAvg demonstrates performance comparable to standard Federated Averaging (FedAvg) and Federated Proximal (FedProx) across the evaluated architectures and achieves superior performance within the LSTM-AE architecture. TruFedAvg, applied within the FedProx framework (TruFedAvgProx), achieves performance comparable to other strategies across all evaluated models. LSTM-AE based TruFedAvg achieves improvements of +3% accuracy, +11% macro-averaged recall, and +9% F1-score on SWaT, and +4% accuracy, +7% macro-averaged recall, and +6% F1-score on WADI, compared to the evaluated FL strategies in global downstream evaluation, with a peak GPU memory usage of 84.48 MB per communication round. These outcomes confirm that trust-aware aggregation improves global model robustness and fault sensitivity in heterogeneous, unlabeled IoT scenarios.

title: LEAF: Layer-Wise Energy-Adaptive Framework for Multi-DNN Real-Time Intermittent Systems.
abstract: Intermittent systems powered by harvested energy face significant challenges due to limited memory and fluctuating energy availability. These challenges are further amplified in real-time applications such as environmental monitoring, where multiple DNN (Deep Neural Network) tasks must satisfy strict timing guarantees and maintain high inference accuracy. Existing solutions based on lightweight static or dynamic DNNs suffer from the lack of energy adaptability and/or excessive memory overhead, making them unsuitable for real-time intermittent systems. To address these limitations, we propose LEAF, a novel layer-wise energy-adaptive framework for real-time intermittent systems executing multiple DNN tasks. LEAF consists of three key components: (i) a runtime-reconfigurable DNN model and training methodology that supports multiple latency–accuracy trade-offs without incurring additional memory overhead; (ii) an energy-aware time budget abstraction that integrates intermittent inference behavior into existing timing guarantee frameworks; and (iii) a runtime scheduling mechanism that jointly leverages the model and abstraction to ensure both timing guarantees and high inference accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that LEAF ensures the timely, energy-aware execution of multiple DNN tasks with higher accuracy compared to existing solutions, validating its effectiveness for real-time intermittent systems.

title: Anchor-Led Swarm Formation and Pose Estimation for 10,000 Pico-Satellites.
abstract: High-density Formation Flight (FF) of 10,000 pico-satellites has been proposed to construct a giant phased-array antenna for Direct-to-Cell (D2C) communication. Realizing this concept under severe cost constraints requires millimeter-level position accuracy and attitude accuracy of less than 0.1°, and planar attitude estimation accuracy of less than 0.1° for the entire FF. This paper introduces a novel architecture where 85 "anchor" satellites equipped with Time-of-Flight (ToF) cameras observe the remaining 10,000 "normal" satellites. We propose a position and attitude estimation method based on lightweight template matching that exploits the known geometry of the satellites. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average position error of less than 1.5 mm and an attitude error of less than 0.1° for normal satellites, even under noisy conditions. Feasibility is also confirmed on a Raspberry Pi 4, which processed a cluster of 217 satellites in approximately 6.5 seconds. Furthermore, the relative measurements among anchors achieve an accuracy of less than 3 mm, which enables the estimation of the formation’s planar model with an angular error of less than 0.02°.

title: A Picture is Worth a Thousand Risks: Inferring Privacy Risks from Home Interior Images via Object-Level Sensitivity Analysis.
abstract: The proliferation of camera-equipped systems in domestic environments, such as Augmented Reality (AR) applications, household robots, smart glasses, and indoor security cameras, raises critical privacy concerns. Beyond capturing users and visitors, these systems record home interiors that may contain objects and contextual cues inadvertently disclosing sensitive information, such as socioeconomic status cues, social or family structure, cultural or religious affiliation, and daily routines or habits. Yet, a systematic understanding of object-level privacy risks in this context remains limited. To address this gap, we conducted a user study with 210 participants, each annotating 18 images from a dataset of 279 home interior images, yielding 541 unique image–object sensitivity assessments. Based on these annotations, we introduce a multidimensional categorization scheme that integrates sensitivity scales, object categories (e.g., windows, bystanders), and information types (e.g., personal data, social circles). We further evaluate the capability of Vision–Language Models (VLMs) to infer sensitive information from images, including content that appears inconspicuous at first glance. Our analysis shows that VLMs correctly identify the objects’ sensitivity degree within images with up to 70%, and few-shot learning techniques further enhance the object sensitivity inference.

title: Artifact: A Picture is Worth a Thousand Risks.
abstract: This artifact releases the annotated dataset used in our study of object-level privacy risks in home interior images. It contains 279 images with manually highlighted objects, including participant-derived sensitivity labels, object categories, and privacy information-type classes. The dataset supports privacy inference analysis via Vision-Language Models (VLMs) by enabling comparative and extended studies of sensitive visual cues in domestic environments.

title: This Is Taking Too Long - Investigating Time as a Proxy for Energy Consumption of LLMs.
abstract: The energy consumption of Large Language Models (LLMs) is raising growing concerns due to their adverse effects on environmental stability and resource use. Yet, these energy costs remain largely opaque to users, especially when models are accessed through an API — a black box in which all information depends on what providers choose to disclose. In this work, we investigate inference time measurements as a proxy to approximate the associated energy costs of API-based LLMs. We ground our approach by comparing our estimations with actual energy measurements from locally hosted equivalents. Our results show that time measurements allow us to infer GPU models for API-based LLMs, grounding our energy cost estimations. Our work aims to create means for understanding the associated energy costs of API-based LLMs, especially for end users.

title: Promises and Risks in using LLMs in Scientific Review.
abstract: The current scientific peer review process faces increasing strain and is becoming difficult to sustain. While large language models (LLMs) can help reviewers by summarizing papers, assessing clarity, and generating timely feedback, the research community remains cautious about relying on LLM-based reviews. In this paper, we explore how LLMs could support and potentially improve parts of the peer review process. We examine both the benefits and limitations by analysing LLM-generated reviews of our own previously published papers, comparing them with human reviewer feedback, identifying points of agreement and disagreement, and considering requirements for the responsible and ethical use of LLMs in peer review.

title: Digital Twin for Intent-driven Edge Networks.
abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are becoming fundamental tools for designing, validating, and operating next generation IoT and edge ecosystems. However, integrating intent based mechanisms into these environments remains challenging due to hardware constraints, heterogeneity, and the operational risks of deploying untested intent policies on physical devices. To address these barriers, this paper presents a Configurable Digital Twin based environment that enables safe, pre deployment testing of intent based IoT and edge networks. The system models virtual Edge Agent Nodes as digital counterparts of physical devices and incorporates an Intent Parser, Orchestrator, and API Gateway to replicate the full intent translation and task allocation lifecycle. A central contribution is the Configuration Portability Layer, which allows the same configuration files to be used seamlessly across both the virtual DT environment and real hardware deployments. We describe the architecture and workflow of the proposed framework and outline expected performance trends such as improved resource utilization, reduced task execution latency, and predictable scalability derived from DT based orchestration principles. This work provides a low risk, flexible, and extensible foundation for intent based IoT and edge experimentation.

title: CompulsEar: Body-Focused Repetitive Behaviors Detection Using Earable-based Inertial Sensing.
abstract: Body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs) such as nail biting, hair pulling, beard pulling, and face itching are common compulsive habits, affecting approximately 20-30% of the population and often going unnoticed until they cause visible physical and psychological harm. Existing monitoring approaches typically rely on self-report, clinician observation, or camera-based systems, which are intrusive, environment-constrained, or difficult to scale in everyday settings. To address this challenge, we propose CompulsEar, an earable-based framework that employs Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) signals from commercially available earables to detect BFRB episodes in situ. Our system captures characteristic motion patterns associated with four BFRB types (nail biting, beard pulling, hair pulling, and face itching). We conducted a user study with 12 diverse participants, highlighting the potential of earable-based sensing as a non-intrusive and scalable foundation for continuous BFRB monitoring and just-in-time intervention.

title: Keynote - Federated AGI: A Generational Opportunity for Pervasive Computing.
abstract: Current scaling laws indicate that future advances in AI will hinge on access to massive amounts of compute and data. How will we obtain the computing power and data resources required to sustain continued AI progress? I believe all roads lead to federated learning, and approaches of this kind. And, in turn, this change represents the biggest opportunity for pervasive computing in a generation: with the right research priorities and execution, pervasive systems can provide the critical infrastructure for tomorrow’s frontier AI, supplying both compute and data; serving as the missing piece for the AI miracle to continue.The AI world may not realize it yet, but it is ready for this radical change. Today, frontier models are trained on essentially the same web-scraped data and rely on data centers that can only scale through unsustainable capital investment. Instead, pervasive systems of sensors, personal devices, scientific instruments, space satellites, vehicles, and embedded computers offer both a limitless stream of new data and a modular, scalable network of compute. Once resources of this scale and quality are unlocked, today’s AI infrastructure paradigm will not compete. Soon, decentralized and federated techniques built on pervasive systems will be how the strongest LLMs are trained; and in time, how aspirational capabilities like AGI will finally be achieved.In this talk, I will describe why the future of AI will be federated, and describe early solutions from Flower Labs and the Cambridge ML Systems Lab (CaMLSys), which address the technical challenges of this shift and place pervasive computing and communication at the core of how tomorrow’s AI is built.

title: Beyond the Beaten Path: Using Gamification to Expand Urban Crowdsensing Coverage.
abstract: Uneven data coverage is a challenge in location-based crowd sensing. This paper investigates whether gamification can improve data coverage by motivating users to explore less frequently visited areas. Building on concepts of crowd sensing and gamification in the context of promoting changes in human mobility behavior, an online survey was developed. In the ongoing survey (n = 346), participants are presented with route-selection scenarios that vary in travel context and route length. Preliminary insights indicate that user behavior is influenced by a combination of contextual and perceptual factors, while basic gamification components may offer limited leverage for directing exploration. The findings suggest that more adaptive and personalized incentive strategies are needed to achieve a balanced and comprehensive coverage of urban environments in mobility data collection.

title: Degradation of Feature Space in Continual Learning.
abstract: Centralized training is the standard paradigm in deep learning, enabling models to learn from a unified dataset in a single location. In such setup, isotropic feature distributions naturally arise as a mean to support well-structured and generalizable representations. In contrast, continual learning operates on streaming and non-stationary data, and trains models incrementally, inherently facing the well-known plasticity-stability dilemma. In such settings, learning dynamics tends to yield increasingly anisotropic feature space.This arises a fundamental question: should isotropy be enforced to achieve a better balance between stability and plasticity, and thereby mitigate catastrophic forgetting?In this paper, we investigate whether promoting feature-space isotropy can enhance representation quality in continual learning. Through experiments using contrastive continual learning techniques on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 data, we find that isotropic regularization fails to improve, and can in fact degrade, model accuracy in continual settings. Our results highlight essential differences in feature geometry between centralized and continual learning, suggesting that isotropy, while beneficial in centralized setups, may not constitute an appropriate inductive bias for non-stationary learning scenarios.

title: Towards Interpretable Depression Detection: Linking Acoustic Features to DSM-5 Indicators.
abstract: Depression affects millions worldwide, yet diagnosis relies on subjective self-reports that may miss authentic behavior. This paper presents an approach linking speech acoustics to DSM-5 depressive-behavior indicators through a transparent Linkage Framework. Unlike black-box models, the framework explicitly maps acoustic features (pitch variability, pauses, speech tempo) to clinical indicators, enabling interpretable, indicator-level outputs. The system runs locally on commodity hardware (HW) to preserve privacy. Preliminary evaluation on DAIC-WOZ shows directionally consistent associations between acoustic features and DSM-5 indicators for psychomotor change and concentration difficulty, supporting the design rationale. Future work will validate on longitudinal datasets and extend multimodal integration while maintaining edge constraints.

title: Cross-Domain Passive Channel Charting from Wi-Fi Sensing toward Robust Indoor Positioning.
abstract: Existing channel state information (CSI)-based passive channel charting (PCC) methodology is a cost-effective alternative for robust and ubiquitous positioning technology in indoor spaces, but exhibits a fundamental limitation in that it is extremely susceptible to configurational domain shifts, such as changes in transmitter placement. This susceptibility acts as a critical barrier to large-scale deployment in low-cost, low-resource internet of things (IoT) environments that utilize a limited number of antennas. To address these constraints, a self-supervised learning based PCC framework robust to configurational domain shifts is proposed. The proposed model utilizes a hybrid architecture combining a convolutional neural network (CNN) head and a Transformer encoder within a Siamese network structure. This architecture achieves robustness by directly modeling the fundamental spatio-temporal dynamics of the CSI, instead of extracting explicit domain-invariant features. Evaluation of the model is performed using a real-world dataset. Experimental results clearly demonstrate the superior robustness of the proposed model in low-cost IoT environments by achieving low positioning error and overcoming the severe performance degradation typically observed in general cross-domain scenarios.

title: From Pixels to Reality: Physical-Digital Patch Attacks on Real-World Camera.
abstract: This demonstration presents Digital-Physical Adversarial Attacks (DiPA), a new class of practical adversarial attacks against pervasive camera-based authentication systems, where an attacker displays an adversarial patch directly on a smartphone screen instead of relying on printed artifacts. This digital-only physical presentation enables rapid deployment, removes the need for total-variation regularization, and improves patch transferability in black-box conditions. DiPA leverages an ensemble of state-of-the-art face-recognition models (ArcFace, MagFace, CosFace) to enhance transfer across unseen commercial systems. Our interactive demo shows a real-time dodging attack against a deployed face-recognition camera, preventing authorized users from being recognized while participants dynamically adjust patch patterns and observe immediate effects on the sensing pipeline. We further demonstrate DiPA’s superiority over existing physical attacks in terms of success rate, feature-space distortion, and reductions in detection confidence, highlighting critical vulnerabilities at the intersection of mobile devices, pervasive vision, and sensor-driven authentication infrastructures.

title: Privacy-Preserving Skeleton-Based Analysis of Visitor Behavior in Museums.
abstract: This study uses depth-sensor technology to characterize visitors’ spatial and social behavior, including engagement in museum environments. Museums are complex spaces that serve as centers of learning and social interaction, attracting diverse populations. Traditional methods of studying visitor interaction with exhibits are often intrusive and costly, requiring specially trained personnel to analyze data. To address these challenges, we propose a system to automatically analyze skeleton data collected from an on-site deployed solution using a set of Kinect v2 sensors across exhibition spaces at the Musikinstrumenten-Museum in Berlin. The system captures detailed information on visitor-exhibition interaction through body joints as skeleton data, providing insights into how designated areas and object placement influence engagement. By using raw skeleton data to derive high-level features, such as dwell time, proximity, pointing gestures, and qualitative observations of group dynamics, we compute spatial and behavioral metrics of visitors while avoiding the storage of identifiable audio or video data and aiming to preserve visitor privacy. The depth camera system enables tracking and displaying visitor interactions, offering a non-intrusive, interactive way to measure attention and engagement. With this study, we demonstrate the feasibility of skeleton-based sensing for automated unobtrusive assessment of human behavior indoors.

title: Addressing Extra Voices and Background Noise in Continuous Speech Monitoring: A Case Study on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
abstract: Continuous speech monitoring using smartphones and smartwatches offers numerous opportunities to detect and predict health deterioration. However, the algorithms used to deliver these benefits must account for the realities of periodic audio recording in the wild, including other voices and overlapping noise. To address the former without clean sample voice recordings, we use speaker diarization to identify the person who speaks the most throughout a given day. To address the latter without compromising the validity of extracted speech features, we leverage the intuition that a reliable feature should remain unaltered by a noise-reduction technique when background noise is minimal. We examine both techniques in the context of a longitudinal dataset collected from 16 patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) over roughly 3 months. Our best model achieved an AUROC of 0.86 when predicting the presence of respiratory symptoms, outperforming baseline models that rely solely on voice activity detection and noise reduction.

title: Artifact: Addressing Extra Voices and Background Noise in Continuous Speech Monitoring.
abstract: This artifact provides the modular software framework underlying the contributions of our PerCom 2026 paper. We present a pipeline designed to identify acoustic features that are either robust to noise degradation or enhanced by noise-reduction algorithms. To facilitate reproducibility and ease of use, we provide a Dockerized environment that automates the installation of complex dependencies, including Google VisQOL and the Bazel build system. To support technical experimentation and adaptation to new domains, this codebase allows researchers to swap feature extractors, filters, and quality measures.

title: A Lightweight Model-Driven 4D Radar Framework for Pervasive Human Detection in Harsh Conditions.
abstract: Pervasive sensing in industrial and underground environments is severely constrained by airborne dust, smoke, confined geometry, and metallic structures, which rapidly degrade optical and LiDAR-based perception. Elevation-resolved 4D millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar offers strong resilience to such conditions, yet there remains a limited understanding of how to process its sparse and anisotropic point clouds for reliable human detection in enclosed, visibility-degraded spaces. This paper presents a fully model-driven 4D radar perception framework designed for real-time execution on embedded edge hardware. The system uses radar as its sole perception modality and integrates domain-aware multi-threshold filtering, ego-motion–compensated temporal accumulation, KD-tree Euclidean clustering with Doppler-aware refinement, and a rule-based 3D classifier. The framework is evaluated in a dust-filled enclosed trailer and in real underground mining tunnels, and in the tested scenarios the radar-based detector maintains stable pedestrian identification as camera and LiDAR modalities fail under severe visibility degradation. These results suggest that the proposed model-driven approach provides robust, interpretable, and computationally efficient perception for safety-critical applications in harsh industrial and subterranean environments.

title: QPilot: Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Scheduling for Object-Sparse MOT.
abstract: Edge computing plays a key role in smart-city deployments. Deploying AI models on edge devices reduces latency and privacy concerns. This work proposes QPilot, a reinforcement-learning-based adaptive model-switching method that dynamically selects detection models of different sizes for multi-object tracking (MOT) inference to balance efficiency and accuracy according to device compute capacity and scene complexity. In object-sparse scenarios, it improves tracking accuracy with only a small additional computational cost and achieves an optimal efficiency–accuracy trade-off in MOT. We validated the method on multiple hardware platforms, showing strong cross-device adaptability as well as feasibility and promise for edge environments.

title: Keynote: LLMs and Physical Simulations for Sensor Based Context Recognition in Open Ended Settings.
abstract: Keynote AbstractGenerative AI is attracting rapidly growing interest in sensor-based human activity and context recognition. Yet, its impact in this domain remains far less transformative than in computer vision, where contemporary foundation models can reliably produce accurate descriptions for a wide range of arbitrary visual scenes. The prospect of an analogous capability for arbitrary "sensor scenes" is highly compelling, but, despite an expanding body of research and encouraging early results, it is still far from being realized in practice.This talk will analyze the fundamental reasons behind the discrepancy between the remarkable progress in vision-centric generative AI and the comparatively modest gains observed in sensor-based context and activity recognition, including issues of the variability of the input space, data heterogeneity, limited large-scale labeled corpora, weak semantic grounding of sensor signals, and challenges in cross-modal generalization. Building on this analysis, the talk will outline how a combination of appropriately adapted multimodal generative models tightly coupled with physics-informed simulation and sensor-aware representation learning can solve those problems enabling more robust, generalizable, and scalable activity and context recognition systems.

title: GAP: A Browser-Only Toolkit for Evaluating Multimodal RAG.
abstract: We present GAP, an open-source, zero-install, browser-only toolkit that automatically evaluates Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) systems on real engineering formula reasoning. Users simply upload structured JSON predictions produced by any MRAG pipeline; GAP instantly computes three orthogonal metrics against 200 expert-crafted questions derived from 10 authoritative technical documents (standards, datasheets, and manuals): (1) Ground Formula: symbolic correctness of extracted LaTeX formulas, (2) Answer Accuracy: numerical or algebraic correctness of the final solution, (3) Provenance Accuracy: faithfulness of cited document and page. Evaluation of eight frontier multimodal MLLMs reveals a universal pathology: provenance accuracy exceeds 98%, yet formula grounding and answer accuracy collapse below 7%. Current MRAG systems reliably locate the correct page but almost always hallucinate or mangle the underlying mathematics. Running entirely client-side, GAP provides the first standardized, reproducible, and instantly accessible way to quantify symbolic reliability in quantitative engineering tasks. The code and online demo of the GAP MRAG evaluation toolkit can be found here.

title: Gesture recognition and hand pose tracking using wearable mmWave radars.
abstract: We address the recognition and tracking of hand pose via a wrist-worn mmWave sensor. Particularly, the radar monitors the motion of the flexor tendons on the lower part of the wrist. By using a 3D-Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model, we achieved a mean detection accuracy of 90.6% on a 10-gesture dataset that was collected from 11 participants and split into separate training, validation and test sets. For person-independent classification, we trained the model via leave-one-person-out cross-validation on a 10 participants dataset and achieved only a mean accuracy of 32.0% with std of 14.4%pt, as well as large variations between subjects. We note the limitations of this system, e.g., the need for calibration for a new user, and address these issues by presenting an analysis of the dataset and proposing ways to further improve the model’s performance. Specifically, dataset statistics suggest that the whole Intermediate Frequency (IF) signal bandwidth and Doppler velocity range were not fully utilized when the samples were recorded. Finally, we have made the gesture dataset publicly available.

title: Hardware-Assisted Detection of DoS Attacks in log2N Fabrics for Pervasive IoT Networks.
abstract: Pervasive and IoT systems can use multi-plane log2N switching fabrics in resource-constrained backbone devices. When the number of planes is reduced, these fabrics become blockable and require advanced control algorithms to maintain acceptable loss levels. However, an adversary can intentionally generate sequences of connection requests that force the fabric into highly congested states, increasing the loss coefficient and degrading the performance of legitimate traffic.This work presents a hardware-assisted method for detecting and mitigating such attacks. A graph and matrix-based model of the switching fabric is implemented on a NetFPGA platform, enabling real-time analysis of state evolution and identification of adversarial patterns derived from known worst-case sequences. The controller can adapt its routing strategy to avoid attacker-induced blocking states.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Digital Twin as a Virtual Platform for Security Analysis in log2 N Switching Fabrics.
abstract: If switching fabrics meet strict nonblocking conditions, they can realize every possible connection configuration without blocking, but at the cost of a large number of planes. In cost-sensitive scenarios, fewer planes are used and a sophisticated control algorithm has to trade off blocking probability against hardware cost. In such a setting, an adversary can inject carefully crafted connection requests that drive the fabric into highly disadvantageous states and artificially increase the loss coefficient.This paper proposes a digital-twin-based analysis platform for log2N switching fabrics. The physical twin is a hardware controller implemented in FPGA, while the digital twin reuses the same matrix-based state representation and graph models of the fabric, and can be driven both by live telemetry and by tracebased simulation. The twin is used to detect attack patterns, to study the trajectory of internal states, and to design improved control strategies without placing additional latency in the data path. We explain how the physical and digital twins are coupled, discuss how monitoring can follow a highly optimized hardware controller without slowing it down, and outline how the digital twin can suggest temporary changes of controller parameters that mitigate detected attacks.

title: Hardware log2N Network with Matrix-Based Control and Alternate-Path Routing.
abstract: Optical I/O is moving from long-haul links into the shortest reaches of AI/ML systems-within racks, servers, and even single compute packages-where electrical interconnects are increasingly limited by reach, bandwidth density, and energy. Recent co-packaged optical I/O demonstrations (e.g., Intel’s Optical Compute Interconnect chiplet) indicate a practical path to multi-terabit, energy-efficient links, but scaling from point-to-point optics to many-node short-reach systems reintroduces classic fabric-control problems: blocking behavior, path selection, and fast distributed admission control. This demo presents a network of an FPGA-based controllers for a multi-plane photonic log2N switching fabric, where fabric occupancy and routing decisions are represented as matrices and updated incrementally on connection setup/teardown. Decision tables enable one-cycle admission decisions in the fast path, while parallel hardware recomputation maintains consistency after state changes. A software "digital twin" visualizes per-plane utilization, routing rationale, and overload/DoS-like traffic patterns in real time, enabling interactive exploration of blocking/nonblocking trade-offs and alternative-path routing.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Security Risks in Multi-Hop Preconfigured Remote Environments for IoT and IIoT Networks.
abstract: Many IoT and Industrial IoT (IIoT) deployments rely on multi-hop remote access with persistent terminal multiplexers such as tmux. While this greatly improves operational continuity and single-user access to scarce resources (e.g., serial ports or JTAG), it can also conceal mixed chains of secure SSH and insecure Telnet or covert channels. In such preconfigured environments, users attaching to an existing tmux session may unknowingly route sensitive traffic through an unprotected intermediate hop, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks on IoT and IIoT management paths. This paper presents concrete scenarios, discusses how SSH tunnelling further obscures the true communication route, and contrasts misuse with legitimate tmux-based workflows. We conclude with auditing and configuration recommendations to align multi-hop remote access with secure-by-design principles for IoT and IIoT networks.

title: Passenger Flow Estimation for Urban Rail: Meta-Learning Approach with Mobile Network Data.
abstract: Accurate estimation of station-to-station passenger flows in urban rail networks is essential for operations, planning, and congestion management. Mobile network data offer a scalable and privacy-preserving alternative to ticketing or sensor data, but base-station logs are noisy, incomplete, and misaligned with railway infrastructure, leading to sparse coverage, missing logs, and "cold-start" lines with little historical data. We tackle these issues with a two-stage framework based on anonymized mobile network statistics. First, a rule-based system built on Mobile Spatial Statistics infers hourly passenger flows on station-to-station edges, and a macroscopic analysis on the Osaka Metro network shows that it reproduces realistic spatial and temporal demand patterns. Second, we refine and impute these estimates using an Attentive Neural Process (ANP) that treats OD estimation as a meta-learning problem over spatiotemporal episodes, conditioning on context edge–time pairs and predicting flows for target pairs via attention over edge-level features, without explicit graph message passing. Experiments on Osaka Metro under three scenarios—random splits, held-out lines (cold-start), and held-out edges (coverage gaps)—show that ANP consistently outperforms k-nearest neighbors, a multilayer perceptron, and a graph neural network, reducing RMSE by more than 60% in the held-out line setting and enabling robust, transferable passenger flow estimation under severe data sparsity.

title: The Role of Transformers and Positional Encoding in Detecting Cyclic Patterns from Wearables Data.
abstract: Human behavior follows hidden biological rhythms that shape mental and physical health. Using mobile and wearable data, we compare classic rhythm-based features with transformer models that learn temporal structure through Positional Encoding. We find that transformers often perform better, especially on longer and more regular data, but are less interpretable, highlighting a trade-off between accuracy and insight.

title: Stationarity-Aware QoS Prediction for Platooning in V2X Networks.
abstract: The advancement of 5G and emerging 6G technologies is enabling Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication systems to support applications such as platooning, advanced driving, and remote operations, etc. These applications require low-latency communication and ability to offload computationally intensive tasks, from resource-constrained vehicles to edge or cloud servers. Effective task offloading depends on accurate Quality of Service (QoS) prediction in highly dynamic vehicular environments. We present a stationarity-aware two-pipeline architecture for predictive QoS and proactive task offloading for a vehicle platooning use case. The master pipeline performs stationarity checks, dynamic clustering, and end-to-end QoS prediction, while the invoked pipeline handles offloading and execution of tasks. To improve safety and coordination, a stationarity-aware clustering technique creates platoons based on network and vehicle data. Our framework improves the accuracy of QoS prediction for following vehicles by using earlier measurements from leader vehicles, allowing for reliable offloading decisions. The results indicate increased decision efficiency, that helps for robust resource management in V2X networks of the future.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Can Floor Reflections Enable Absolute Robot Localization? A Single-Speaker TDoA Approach.
abstract: In smart homes and offices, the deployment of autonomous mobile robots is accelerating. Accurate self-localization is essential for these robots; however, existing approaches still struggle to achieve reliable absolute positioning in everyday environments. SLAM is indispensable for local navigation but suffers from drift, degraded performance in feature-poor spaces, and cannot provide absolute coordinates, while emerging single-anchor methods often require specialized hardware like UWB. To address these limitations and complement SLAM with an absolute global constraint, we propose a ubiquitous localization method leveraging acoustic TDoA from a single speaker via floor reflections. This study investigates whether the weak geometric constraints derived solely from floor reflections can enable accurate localization when fused with odometry via a Particle Filter. Real-world experiments demonstrate a converged accuracy of 0.18 m. By utilizing everyday audio infrastructure, this approach significantly lowers deployment barriers for service robots.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Accelerating Model-Free Reinforcement Learning for HVAC Control with an LLM as a Policy Teacher.
abstract: Balancing energy efficiency and occupant comfort in Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) control is essential for quality of life. Model-free reinforcement learning (MFRL) is a promising approach, offering adaptability and optimality by learning policies directly without environment-specific models. However, MFRL suffers from poor sample efficiency during early exploration, making it impractical for real-world HVAC operation. To address this, we adapt the LLM-guided RL paradigm—typically used in discrete robotics—to the continuous HVAC domain. We model the LLM’s guidance as a continuous Gaussian distribution and integrate it into Soft Actor-Critic via a KL divergence regularization term. This enables the agent to leverage common-sense knowledge for efficient exploration in continuous action spaces. Experiments using EnergyPlus show that our method reduces the training steps to approximately one-fifth of standard MFRL, achieving policies that effectively balance comfort and energy efficiency. These results highlight the potential of LLM-guided MFRL for practical, energy-efficient control systems.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: On-Device AI for Voice-Driven Multi-Parameter Health-Risk Monitoring.
abstract: The proliferation of digital health systems has generated vast amounts of sensitive patient data, unlocking opportunities for enhanced disease prediction, diagnosis, and treatment via advanced analytics. However, preventive telemedicine demands continuous monitoring for proactive, personalized care, where traditional methods often fail to detect rapid physiological changes, particularly in low-connectivity or remote environments. This gap poses significant risks for patients with chronic or post-surgical conditions, necessitating robust, offline-capable solutions.Building on our prior voice-driven mobile health application, this paper integrates an on-device AI model to enable real-time, multi-parameter health-risk prediction on smartphones. A lightweight Deep Neural Network (DNN), deployed via Tensor-Flow Lite, executes locally to generate personalized risk scores, triggering immediate voice alerts and on-screen warnings upon detecting abnormal patterns. In addition, the platform supports text-or voice-based entry of six vital signs and securely stores all measurements and predictions for clinical review through a cloud backend. By combining natural voice interaction, offline reliability, wearable integration, and efficient on-device inference, this scalable and privacy-preserving solution enables continuous monitoring and early anomaly detection in both urban and rural areas.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Keynote: Trends in Space Technologies for Expanding the Potential of Terrestrial Pervasive Computing.
abstract: Space development and utilization have changed significantly over the past decade, and this transformation is expected to continue. Whereas spacecraft were traditionally designed as expensive stand alone systems operated in limited numbers, reductions in launch cost, such as those achieved by SpaceX Falcon 9 and Starship, together with the increasing use of commercial technologies, have enabled the rapid deployment of large scale small satellite constellations, exemplified by Starlink. These trends are often referred to as NewSpace, yet their background and implications are not widely understood outside the space community. This keynote first reviews how space systems are evolving from isolated platforms to systems that are continuously integrated with terrestrial information and communication technologies. Recent advances such as low Earth orbit satellite constellations, the use of commercial off the shelf technology in orbit, inter satellite links, and Non Terrestrial Networks that integrate satellite communications with terrestrial cellular networks are introduced in a manner accessible to audiences without prior expertise in space systems. The talk then highlights how these advances expand the capabilities of terrestrial pervasive computing, in which computation, communication, and sensing operate seamlessly without user awareness, as required by applications such as autonomous driving, the Internet of Things, and Cyber Physical Systems. Examples include services that become possible only when previously unconnected regions are integrated into information and communication technology systems, as well as the utilization of wide area and high frequency remote sensing data from space. Finally, the keynote introduces the speaker’s work on formation flying and satellite clustering as new spacecraft operation paradigms, in which multiple spacecraft operate cooperatively as an invisible extension of terrestrial information and communication technology infrastructure.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Wearable-Enabled Screening of RBD Through HRV-Based Machine Learning.
abstract: Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder (RBD) is one of the strongest prodromal markers of neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's disease. However, its current diagnosis relies on overnight video-polysomnography, which is costly, intrusive, and unsuitable for population-level screening. Heart Rate Variability (HRV), which reflects autonomic regulation, offers a promising non-invasive alternative based on wearable ECG sensing, enabling scalable detection in pervasive healthcare environments.This PhD research investigates the feasibility of HRV-based automatic RBD screening through Machine Learning (ML). Four polysomnography datasets (184 subjects) were analyzed to evaluate the robustness of HRV features under realistic conditions. A comprehensive set of 528 time, frequency, and nonlinear-domain attributes was extracted from FullNight and SleepOnly ECG segments, and multiple ML pipelines were trained and optimized for two binary tasks: healthy vs. RBD, and non-RBD (healthy+OSAS) vs. RBD.Results show that HRV biomarkers enable accurate discrimination, achieving F1-scores above 90% in healthy-RBD classification and above 80% even when confounding sleep disorders are included. Moreover, stage-agnostic FullNight extraction improved generalization across heterogeneous datasets, supporting wearable deployment without expert scoring.These findings highlight the potential of autonomic-based pervasive screening for prodromal neurodegeneration and motivate further validation on real-world wearable data toward home-based early diagnosis.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: A Benchmarking Framework for Privacy-Preserving Human Pose Estimation on Edge Devices.
abstract: Deploying human pose estimation (HPE) pipelines in privacy-aware settings requires processing sensitive data close to the point of acquisition, as set out in regulations such as the AI Act. Edge devices can meet this requirement, but their limited resources modify the impact of privacy mechanisms, hardware capacity, and scene complexity on latency. This paper presents a framework that jointly analyzes latency and privacy in HPE pipelines executed on edge architectures. We consider two representative scenarios: i) all the pipeline stages on the acquisition device; ii) acquisition and obfuscation on the camera, with inference on a separate edge node. We present the framework by evaluating each scenario with deployments based on three state-of-the-art HPE models (MoveNet, YOLO-Pose, and OpenPose), three representative hardware configurations, and three levels of scene complexity based on the number of subjects and visual entropy. For each deployment, the framework estimates stage-level and end-to-end latency distributions, obtains the probability of completing the pipeline within task-specific deadlines, and the attainable privacy level. Our framework also generates reliability-privacy-cost maps, a decision support tool that relates improvements in timing and privacy to the cost of implementing or upgrading a deployment. A surveillance case study illustrates how the framework helps design or adapt privacy-preserving edge infrastructures.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Hierarchical Silent Command Recognition on Earables: A Multistage Learning Approach.
abstract: Silent communication is vital in high-noise environments such as construction sites, where conventional voice interfaces often fail. We present a silent speech recognition (SSR) system on the OpenEarable platform, combining ear canal pressure sensing with inertial measurement units (IMUs). We collected a dataset of 14 commands, including seven essential control words (e.g., Stop, Go) and their phonetically similar counterparts (e.g., Stop, Top), from 20 participants. The dataset is used for training various machine learning models. The results show that IMU-based sensing is the primary driver of robust, noise-resilient SSR, achieving 91.95% F1-score by capturing subtle jaw and head movements. Pressure-only sensing underperforms, while multimodal fusion with CNNs improves performance further. To enhance real-world deployability, we propose a binary-plus-multiclass pipeline that first filters intended commands from phonetically similar inputs. Our findings show that deeper CNNs and natural head gestures provide additional robustness. Deployment profiling confirms real-time inference (402–650 ms latency) on embedded hardware.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Quantification Of Correctness Of Squat From Real-Time 3D Posture Evaluation.
abstract: Squat is one of the most widely-adopted exercises for strengthening the lower body, especially quadriceps and ham-strings. If not performed correctly, especially as a part of rehabilitation while recovering from a lower body injury, it can cause lower back pain, severe knee injuries, and muscle imbalance. We present a fully automated, 3D posture monitoring and assessment system which works in real-time using Google’s Mediapipe pose land marking, powered with our customized scoring based on the type of squat prescribed by a physiotherapist. Our assessment model calculates clinically relevant parameters like squat depth, squat bias, stance width etc. as defined in literature for a certain prescribed variant of squat, which itself can be recorded as a reference profile in the system by the physiotherapist extracted from sample repetitions performed by them personalized for their patient. A score report is generated for a squat session, quantifying the quality of squat being performed by the patient compared against the prescribed variant. The comparison score is generated on-device using sigmoid-based metric customized for every parameter, without requiring heavy computations or prior dataset like in a DL-based assessment model. The pipeline is robust to environmental and demographic factors. In this demonstration, we aim to show the capability of real-time scoring using multiple reference profiles for different squat variants at the venue. This is a step forward towards a safer exercising and reliable remote rehabilitation monitoring.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: On the Design of Tiny ECG Encoder for Biometric Applications.
abstract: Biometric identification systems utilize unique physiological and behavioral traits, including fingerprints, iris patterns, voice, and facial features, to provide secure and convenient authentication resistant to falsification and unauthorized sharing. With the growth of digital transformation and cyber-security threats, these systems are increasingly deployed across domains such as banking, healthcare, mobile devices to ensure reliable identification and mitigate the risks of fraud and forgery. In this paper, we propose a system to identify the most optimal latent representation of ECG beats using an auto-generated and optimized encoder architecture for biometric applications. This will help us identify the unique signatures of an individual in an efficient and scalable way, suitable for customized edge platforms. It also ensures that the resulting system is effective in terms of both accuracy and device resources, while facilitating fast and easy deployment in real-time, low-power systems. This also allows smaller groups to adapt the systems quickly to authorized users, making the security system more reliable and independent of large databases for training and identification. The proposed system extracts latent features from ECG signals with an encoder of size less than 500 kB and identifies authorised users with a high accuracy, simultaneously demonstrating a significant reduction in size compared to large-scale autoencoders, enabling easy deployment and retraining on low-compute environments.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: Efficient Memory Usage For Edge FaaS Platforms.
abstract: Function as a Service (FaaS) is a great fit for data and event processing in Edge environments. These environments are characterized by resource-constrained devices that require efficient memory usage optimizations. Existing optimization solutions for memory in high-end clusters such as data centers cannot be used in Edge environments because they either depend on unavailable hardware features such as RDMA or require resource-intensive analysis such as periodic memory scanning, compression, or decompression.In this paper, we introduce Extensible RUNtimes (ERUN), a lightweight mechanism for existing FaaS runtimes aimed at optimizing memory utilization by reducing the memory usage of idle sandboxes (i.e., those awaiting function execution). ERUN operates through two main actions: Shrink and Expand. The Shrink operation unloads libraries and reclaims memory from the sandboxes, while the Expand operation quickly reloads the libraries when a function is executed. The Expand operation leverages an in-memory store that maintains a single instance of discarded libraries on the node. We implement the ERUN mechanism, which can be applied to any runtime environment, in a Python runtime. We extensively evaluated our prototype in a 10-node Edge cluster using 10 popular FaaS functions. The results show that ERUN reduces idle sandbox memory usage by up to 23.13× and improves the warm-start ratio by 1.38×, with less than 2% overhead on execution time and energy usage.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications

title: BRAIN: Blockchain-Based Reputation Architecture for Interest-flooding Neutralization in NDNs.
abstract: Named Data Networking (NDN) can face critical security vulnerabilities from Interest Flooding Attacks (IFA), where malicious nodes exhaust router resources through excessive requests for nonexistent content. The current existing NDN defense mechanisms lack persistent cross-session accountability, allowing attackers to rejoin networks with clean reputations after disconnection. Meanwhile, blockchain technology promises distributed trust management without centralized authorities, yet traditional blockchain architectures impose prohibitive latency and computational overhead for real-time network security applications. This paper presents a novel Blockchain-based Reputation Architecture and Information Networking (BRAIN) that demonstrates the feasibility of distributed ledger technology (DLT) for network forwarding security. BRAIN utilizes a microchain design with reputation-weighted consensus, localized trust domains, and constant-time per-packet enforcement that maintains accountability across network sessions while achieving sub-second block finality. Our proof-of-concept BRIAN implementation integrates lightweight blockchain operations with NDN’s forwarding plane through reputation-based admission control and graduated enforcement policies. Initial experimental validation demonstrates that BRAIN achieves 97% detection accuracy against coordinated flooding attacks while reducing router resource exhaustion by 93%, with an average latency of 10 milliseconds, representing a 75% improvement over traditional blockchain-enabled network architectures. These preliminary results indicate that blockchain-based reputation management can operate at network-forwarding speeds, opening the possibility of distributed trust mechanisms in latency-sensitive pervasive computing environments.

title: Evaluating Classical Machine Learning Models for Road Surface Classification on Resource-Constrained Microcontrollers.
abstract: Road surface classification is a fundamental capability for smart mobility, infrastructure monitoring, and pervasive sensing systems. This paper investigates the end-to-end deployment of classical Machine Learning (ML) algorithms on an ESP32-S3 microcontroller for real-time road surface classification. Using a balanced dataset of 2,721 samples collected across six bicycle and automotive road-surface conditions, we convert each model into optimized C code and evaluate both classification performance and embedded deployment metrics. Our results characterize the trade-offs between accuracy, memory footprint, and per-sample inference time, providing a comparative assessment of ML algorithms under strict resource constraints. The findings highlight the practical viability of classical ML at the extreme edge and offer guidance for the design of low-cost, infrastructure-independent road-surface sensing systems in pervasive computing environments.

title: Personal Data Ecosystems in Decentralised Clinical Trials.
abstract: The organisation-centric model of data management arguably constrains portability, transparency, and individual agency, limitations that are particularly acute in health research. This paper explores Personal Data Ecosystems (PDEs) as an alternative, specifically within the context of participant discovery for decentralised clinical trials. Building on the ESPRESSO framework for Efficient Search over Personal Repositories – Secure and Sovereign, we explore a decentralised search mechanism that employs Personal Online Datastores (PODs) to facilitate data aggregation and selective sharing, thereby enforcing differential visibility and fine-grained access control. We discuss the performance of this system in the context of privacy-preserving keyword queries across metropolitan-scale cohorts, aiming to merge authoritative centralised records with POD-based streams derived from user-provided wearable and smartphone technologies, which offer unique insights into symptoms and individual performance. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach through a proof-of-concept implementation on HAT/Dataswyft, complementing prior investigations on Solid, and discuss practical challenges such as API governance and structured data indexing. Finally, we outline how PDEs and compute-to-data paradigms may enable self-sovereign AI, enabling federated learning and inference sovereignty. Our findings suggest a trajectory toward secure, participatory, and interoperable health data infrastructures.

title: ReFDrone: One-Shot Indoor Drone 4DoF Estimation via Rolling-Shutter AoA from Floor-Reflected Light.
abstract: Accurate indoor drone four degrees-of-freedom (4DoF) estimation, including both 3D position and heading, is essential for safe flight in GNSS-denied environments, opening up opportunities for fully autonomous IoT applications such as infrastructure inspection and surveillance. Approaches using a built-in camera are attractive due to their low cost and ease of deployment, however, existing methods face key limitations. Visual-Inertial Odometry suffers from drift and often fails in textureless environments, while Visible Light Positioning requires a direct line of sight to ceiling LEDs, which is challenging for drones with a limited field of view. We propose ReFDrone, a system that simultaneously estimates 3D position and heading from a single image using a downward-facing rolling-shutter (RS) landing camera and floor-reflected light from modulated ceiling LEDs. Our core insight is that RS distortion produces spectral lobes in the frequency domain whose orientation directly encodes the angle of arrival (AoA) of the LED. Leveraging this property, ReFDrone extracts AoA from a single RS image, enabling estimation of 2D position and heading from just two LEDs, and derives altitude using a virtual-view image with a distance model. We evaluated ReFDrone under 1296 conditions in 2.5 m x 2.5 m testbed, achieving a 90th percentile 3D position error of 0.335 m and a heading error of 8.101 degrees, demonstrating its accuracy and practicality.
